Source: http://www.marijuananews.com

Posted October 18, 2000
Analysis by Richard Cowan

Last Friday, I posted Media Alert: Watch for New NIDA Study Claiming Animal Tests Prove Marijuana Is Addictive. Great Marketing of Prohibitionist Propaganda. -- describing how NIDA was pushing a report and denying critics the opportunity to see it. They even paid the PRNewswire to distribute it, assuring that it would get the maximum coverage without any chance of criticism.
See
As Predicted, NIDA Buys Its Press Release: " Marijuana has as much potential for abuse … as cocaine and heroin. "

On Sunday, the Media Awareness Project posted the news release from NIDA on this " Latest Research " on marijuana, under the header: 'Marijuana As Addicting As Cocaine and Heroin' with the explanatory prediction, " We made the headline up, but it is what we may expect in newspapers in the days ahead. "

Very close. The BBC website article had the headline " Cannabis 'as addictive as cocaine.' " The London Times headline was " Tests show pot is as 'addictive as heroin' " and the header in London’s otherwise often excellent Independent said, " Marijuana 'is as addictive as heroin'. "

Why was this so predictable?

The substance of the articles was not much better than the headlines. Although no one who was likely to be critical of the study was allowed to see it, the AP did at least call NORML, and were referred to Dr. Lester Grinspoon.So a few papers, including the New York Times, carried a perfunctory effort at " balance. "

" This drug is not addicting. Clinical experience says that, " said Dr. Lester Grinspoon, an emeritus professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School.

The monkey study does not prove otherwise, said Dr. Grinspoon, who is chairman of the board of the NORML Foundation, which promotes medical use of marijuana and ultimately its legalization. "

Dr. Grinspoon laughed when he told me that they had definitely not reported his criticism of NIDA.

Notice that they made very clear that Dr. Grinspoon has a political agenda, but they could never bring themselves to indicate that anyone on the other side might possibly have one, even though NIDA’s bias was recently the subject of an article on Salon.com about NIDA head, Dr. Alan Leshner.
See
The drug war's Tweedledee

The prohibitionist London Times, however, apparently did manage to interview the principle author of the study, Dr. Steven Goldberg, who is quoted as saying, " People who want to decriminalise cannabis should look at these findings closely. "

Oh really? Actually, I couldn’t agree more, but not in the way that he thinks. It is incredibly arrogant and corrupt to think that a study of 4 monkeys, injected with a synthetic version of one ingredient in marijuana has any relevance to social policy. However, his statement shows that there was definitely a political agenda at work here.

And why are Dr. Grinspoon’s policy views relevant, but not Dr. Goldberg’s?

Of course, the same London Times article dutifully reported, " A spokesman for Keith Hellawell, the Government’s anti-drugs co-ordinator, said that he would examine the report closely. ‘It’s a myth to say that cannabis is not harmful and that it is not abused.’ " Nothing is harmless or cannot be abused, including " science. "

In fact, this study proves absolutely nothing about marijuana use by humans. Period. However, it is part of a long-term pattern of media gullibility in what I call NIDA’s " Latest Research " scam.

For decades, the prohibitionists have gotten away with issuing press releases about the " Latest Research " that purports to show some dire consequence of using marijuana, and the media reports them breathlessly, and uncritically. Of this sorry lot, few, if any, are as bad as this latest " Latest Research. "

After all, if marijuana really did have " as much potential for abuse as other drugs of abuse, such as cocaine and heroin, " would we have to find this out from an experiment on 4 stressed-out little monkey’s on an I-V feed?
See
Is marijuana addictive?
and links

Where are the marijuana junkies robbing to pay for their habits? Why did the Drug Czar’s own IOM report say that, " A distinctive marijuana withdrawal syndrome has been identified, but it is mild and short-lived "?

Is this consistent with the claim that marijuana has the same abuse potential as cocaine and heroin?

And if THC is so addictive, how is that the makers of Marinol can claim that it is not?

See
No Evidence That THC Is Addictive Says Maker of Marinol
After 9 Month Study Including Law Enforcement

Is this consistent with the claim that marijuana has the same abuse potential as cocaine and heroin?

Moreover, another example of NIDA’s " Latest Research " game would seem to contradict the latest Latest.
See
New NIDA Sponsored " Latest Research " Shows Competitiveness of Heavy Marijuana Users
Not Impaired When They Stop Smoking – Well, That Is My Interpretation – 2 Versions From Reuters
and links

In that study it was claimed that people who have smoked marijuana daily for many years display more " aggression " playing games when they are going through withdrawal than do " infrequent and former users. "

Taking this study at face value, it would appear that heavy smokers may be a bit irritable when they quit, but is this consistent with the claim that marijuana has the same abuse potential as cocaine and heroin?

Also, NIDA’s own researchers have compared the addictiveness of various drugs and rank marijuana below coffee.
See
The Relative Addictiveness of Drugs According to NIDA's Own Researcher

Is this consistent with the claim that marijuana has the same abuse potential as cocaine and heroin?

Now if this " Latest Research " had been a study on – say – the long-term effect of heavy cannabis on the endocrine system, this would at least be a subject on which common everyday observation would be irrelevant. However, there are huge numbers of people who smoke marijuana regularly, and yet we do not hear about them having uncontrollable cravings or withdrawal when they stop. Everyone knows nicotine addicts who are having problems quitting. Most of us know alcoholics who are unable to stop drinking, but how common is it to find a marijuana user who cannot quit? Is this consistent with the claim that marijuana has the same abuse potential as cocaine and heroin?

If NIDA announced that the " Latest Research " proved that marijuana turned users green, would the media run the story under the headline, " U. S. scientists say… "?

The obvious question would be where are all the green marijuana users? Well, where are all the marijuana addicts?
See
Claim Two: " More Than 120 000 People In The US Seek Treatment Each Year For Their Marijuana Addiction "

In short, seeing through this latest round of the " Latest Research " did not require anything but common sense. But if marijuana addicts are hard to find, common sense in reporting on marijuana is even harder to find.

Almost as hard to find as reports on marijuana arrests.

On Monday, the day that most of the media ran NIDA’s latest, NORML emailed the media a report on the 1999 arrest statistics.
See
NORML Reports: In 1999, A New Record for Marijuana Arrests! 4,175,357 Americans Have Been Arrested During the Clinton Administration.

Have you seen any reports on this?

There have now been over 4 million marijuana arrests under Clinton/Gore, but I can count on the fingers of one hand, the number of times I have seen any reports on the arrest data in the last seven years. When I became National Director of NORML in 1992, Allen St. Pierre and I began NORML’s effort to publicize the arrest numbers. We put them on the letterhead and on virtually everything we sent out.
See
Are people really being arrested for marijuana possession? What happens when someone is arrested?

There has been far more coverage on even the most speculative reports on alleged risks to marijuana use than on the fact that hundreds of thousands of people are being arrested in DEAland every year.


See
Marijuana and " Heart Attack " Report Tells Us More About Media And Politicized Medicine Than About Marijuana. -- 2 Articles
(This one was not a NIDA product.)

The UK media – and certainly the Canadian media -- report their arrest numbers as a part of their national debates on marijuana prohibition. That is a necessary part of any debate, which may explain in part why it is so difficult to get the DEAland politicians even to discuss marijuana prohibition, as opposed to the " scourge of drugs. "
See
Canada's Crime Rate Dropped In 1999 For 8th Consecutive Year Without Creating A Police State. But Marijuana Arrests Continue to Climb. Alcohol Related Violence Soars in UK. Lessons for Everyone.

On the one hand we have a highly speculative story about 4 monkeys. On the other we have hard government data about 4 million people that is certainly not overstated. Which gets the most coverage? No contest.

Why are 4 monkeys in cages more newsworthy than 4 million Americans in cages?

The best two word explanation for marijuana prohibition is still bad journalism. Disgraceful.
See
Author of Ottawa Citizen Series on Prohibition Blames The Media for the Drug War. Great Journalism Is The Antidote.

Welcome to the age of the Internet, the world is watching Big Brother.

Be sure and log on to www.pot-tv.net for the 420 MarijuanaNews with Richard Cowan weekdays at any time after 4:20PM Pacific. The current programs are now available " on demand. " And if you miss any broadcasts, they are still available in the Archives.
